verses.english: On Immersion at Jīvaka’s Mango Grove

verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati jīvakambavane.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in Jīvaka’s Mango Grove.
There the Buddha addressed the mendicants:
For a mendicant with immersion, things become truly clear.

verses.pali: Cakkhuṁ aniccanti yathābhūtaṁ okkhāyati, rūpā aniccāti yathābhūtaṁ okkhāyati, cakkhuviññāṇaṁ aniccanti yathābhūtaṁ okkhāyati, cakkhusamphasso aniccoti yathābhūtaṁ okkhāyati, yampidaṁ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi aniccanti yathābhūtaṁ okkhāyati …pe…
verses.english: It becomes truly clear that the eye, sights, eye consciousness, and eye contact are impermanent. And it also becomes truly clear that the painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on eye contact is impermanent.
It becomes truly clear that the ear … nose … tongue … body …

verses.pali: mano aniccoti yathābhūtaṁ okkhāyati, dhammā aniccāti yathābhūtaṁ okkhāyati …pe…
verses.english: mind, ideas, mind consciousness, and mind contact are impermanent.

verses.pali: yampidaṁ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṁ sukhaṁ vā dukkhaṁ vā adukkhamasukhaṁ vā tampi aniccanti yathābhūtaṁ okkhāyati.
verses.english: And it also becomes truly clear that the painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling that arises dependent on mind contact is impermanent.
For a mendicant with immersion, things become truly clear.”
